newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian says plan saves $800 mln over 4 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Canadian says plan saves $800 mln over 4 yrs.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp's survival plan announced on Friday is aimed at adding C$800 million to the struggling carrier's bottom line over four years, Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson said.
The plan would include a 10-percent wage cut from employees, major restructuring of its domestic and international capacity and fee concessions from 33-percent owner AMR Corp.
"Canadian has had a history of chronic losses. We have to address it and we are addressing it," Benson told a packed news conference at the company's head office.
Benson said the moves, which require approval from Canadian's unions and AMR, would slowly bring the carrier to profitability without revenue growth.
The details were not negotiable, he said.
Canadian aims to cut its domestic capacity by 11 percent, but use the Canada-U.S. Open Skies agreement and expanded Vancouver hub to bolster United States and Asian traffic and yields.
The airline is poised for a 1996 loss that will be less than last year, but still "significant," Benson said. Canadian lost C$195 million in 1995.
He said the plans announced on Friday could be implemented quickly enough to avert a cash deficiency that was predicted for the first quarter of 1997.
Canadian said it would ask its employees and other stakeholders for approval by the end of November.

"This current deadline is an essential one. We do not want our customers worried about the airline," he said. "We believe we need to address these issues and confirm where we're going before the end of November," Benson said.
